source_coverage: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
instructions: Decide per CONSOLIDATION_POLICY.md: one of CANONICALIZE | EQUIVALENCE_GROUP | CROSSWALK_ONLY | RELATE_ONLY | KEEP_SEPARATE | DEPRECATE_DERIVED. If merging, author an English canonical per AUTHORING_POLICY.md and set mapping_strength per source. Do NOT invent USACM/SDT values. Do NOT delete raw records.

members.description: Use unique passwords for all enterprise assets. Do not use the same password for multiple assets.
Require all external or remote access to the enterprise network, such as VPN, to use Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).
Require Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for all administrative access to enterprise assets.
Configure PAM to enforce strong password creation requirements (complexity, minimum length) and password expiration policies.
Configure the account lockout policy to mitigate brute force credential attacks (e.g., lockout after 5 failed attempts for 15 minutes).
Cybersecurity requirements for identity and access management of the entity shall include the following as a minimum: 2.2.3.1 Single-factor authentication based on username and password.

Cybersecurity requirements for protection of the email serviceofthe entity shall include the following as a minimum: 2.4.3.1 Analyzing and filtering email messages (specifically phishing emails and spam emails) using modern and advanced email protection techniques and mechanisms.

Cybersecurity requirements for the entity’s network security management shall include the following as a minimum: ‫ﻣﻘﻴﺪ‬ 2.5.3.1 Logical or physical isolation and segmentation of network segments in a secure manner which is required to control relevant cybersecurity risks, using firewall and defense-in-depth principle.
Cybersecurity requirements for protection of external web applications of the entity shall include the following as a minimum: 2.15.3.1 Use of web application firewall.

Verify that the client (as the relying party) mitigates ID Token replay attacks.

members.source_section: Requirement V11.4.3 (V11.4 Hashing and Hash-based Functions)
members.description: Verify that hash functions used in digital signatures, as part of data authentication or data integrity are collision resistant and have appropriate bit-lengths.

members.source_section: Requirement V12.1.3 (V12.1 General TLS Security Guidance)

members.source_section: Requirement V12.3.5 (V12.3 General Service to Service Communication Security)
members.title_draft: V12.3.5 — General Service to Service Communication Security
members.description: Verify that services communicating internally within a system (intra-service communications) use strong authentication to ensure that each endpoint is verified.
Verify that communications between backend application components that don't support the application's standard user session mechanism, including APIs, middleware, and data layers, are authenticated.
Verify that if a credential has to be used for service authentication, the credential being used by the consumer is not a default credential (e.g., root/root or admin/admin).
Verify that all authentication operations are logged, including successful and unsuccessful attempts.

Verify that Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (SRTP) authentication is checked at the media server to prevent Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP) injection attacks from leading to either a Denial of Service condition or audio or video media insertion into media streams.

Verify that application documentation defines how controls such as rate limiting, anti-automation, and adaptive response, are used to defend against attacks such as credential stuffing and password brute force.
Verify that a list of context-specific words is documented in order to prevent their use in passwords.

Verify that, if the application includes multiple authentication pathways, these are all documented together with the security controls and authentication strength which must be consistently enforced across them.
Verify that user set passwords are at least 8 characters in length although a minimum of 15 characters is strongly recommended.
Verify that users can change their password.
Verify that password change functionality requires the user's current and new password.

Verify that passwords submitted during account registration or password change are checked against an available set of, at least, the top 3000 passwords which match the application's password policy, e.g.
Verify that passwords of any composition can be used, without rules limiting the type of characters permitted.
Verify that password input fields use type=password to mask the entry.
Verify that "paste" functionality, browser password helpers, and external password managers are permitted.
Verify that the application verifies the user's password exactly as received from the user, without any modifications such as truncation or case transformation.
Verify that passwords of at least 64 characters are permitted.
Verify that a user's password stays valid until it is discovered to be compromised or the user rotates it.
Verify that the documented list of context specific words is used to prevent easy to guess passwords being created.
Verify that passwords submitted during account registration or password changes are checked against a set of breached passwords.
Verify that controls to prevent attacks such as credential stuffing and password brute force are implemented according to the application's security documentation.
Verify that default user accounts (e.g., "root", "admin", or "sa") are not present in the application or are disabled.
Verify that either a multi-factor authentication mechanism or a combination of single-factor authentication mechanisms, must be used in order to access the application.
Verify that, if the application includes multiple authentication pathways, there are no undocumented pathways and that security controls and authentication strength are enforced consistently.
Verify that users are notified of suspicious authentication attempts (successful or unsuccessful).
Verify that email is not used as either a single-factor or multi-factor authentication mechanism.
Verify that users are notified after updates to authentication details, such as credential resets or modification of the username or email address.
Verify that valid users cannot be deduced from failed authentication challenges, such as by basing on error messages, HTTP response codes, or different response times.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.4.1 (V6.4 Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery)
members.title_draft: V6.4.1 — Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery
members.description: Verify that system generated initial passwords or activation codes are securely randomly generated, follow the existing password policy, and expire after a short period of time or after they are initially used.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.4.2 (V6.4 Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery)
members.title_draft: V6.4.2 — Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery
members.description: Verify that password hints or knowledge-based authentication (so-called "secret questions") are not present.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.4.3 (V6.4 Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery)
members.title_draft: V6.4.3 — Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery
members.description: Verify that a secure process for resetting a forgotten password is implemented, that does not bypass any enabled multi-factor authentication mechanisms.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.4.4 (V6.4 Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery)
members.title_draft: V6.4.4 — Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery
members.description: Verify that if a multi-factor authentication factor is lost, evidence of identity proofing is performed at the same level as during enrollment.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.4.5 (V6.4 Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery)
members.title_draft: V6.4.5 — Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery
members.description: Verify that renewal instructions for authentication mechanisms which expire are sent with enough time to be carried out before the old authentication mechanism expires, configuring automated reminders if necessary.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.4.6 (V6.4 Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery)
members.title_draft: V6.4.6 — Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery
members.description: Verify that administrative users can initiate the password reset process for the user, but that this does not allow them to change or choose the user's password.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.5.1 (V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements)
members.description: Verify that lookup secrets, out-of-band authentication requests or codes, and time-based one-time passwords (TOTPs) are only successfully usable once.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.5.2 (V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements)
members.description: Verify that, when being stored in the application's backend, lookup secrets with less than 112 bits of entropy (19 random alphanumeric characters or 34 random digits) are hashed with an approved password storage hashing algorithm that incorporates a 32-bit random salt.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.5.3 (V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements)
members.description: Verify that lookup secrets, out-of-band authentication code, and time-based one-time password seeds, are generated using a Cryptographically Secure Pseudorandom Number Generator (CSPRNG) to avoid predictable values.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.5.4 (V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements)
members.description: Verify that lookup secrets and out-of-band authentication codes have a minimum of 20 bits of entropy (typically 4 random alphanumeric characters or 6 random digits is sufficient).

members.source_section: Requirement V6.5.5 (V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements)
members.description: Verify that out-of-band authentication requests, codes, or tokens, as well as time-based one-time passwords (TOTPs) have a defined lifetime.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.5.6 (V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements)
members.description: Verify that any authentication factor (including physical devices) can be revoked in case of theft or other loss.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.5.7 (V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements)
members.description: Verify that biometric authentication mechanisms are only used as secondary factors together with either something you have or something you know.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.5.8 (V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements)
members.description: Verify that time-based one-time passwords (TOTPs) are checked based on a time source from a trusted service and not from an untrusted or client provided time.

Verify that authentication mechanisms using the Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) to deliver One-time Passwords (OTPs) via phone or SMS are offered only when the phone number has previously been validated, alternate stronger methods (such as Time based One-time Passwords) are also offered, and the
Verify that out-of-band authentication requests, codes, or tokens are bound to the original authentication request for which they were generated and are not usable for a previous or subsequent one.
Verify that a code based out-of-band authentication mechanism is protected against brute force attacks by using rate limiting.
Verify that, where push notifications are used for multi-factor authentication, rate limiting is used to prevent push bombing attacks.
Verify that the certificates used to verify cryptographic authentication assertions are stored in a way protects them from modification.
Verify that the challenge nonce is at least 64 bits in length, and statistically unique or unique over the lifetime of the cryptographic device.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.8.1 (V6.8 Authentication with an Identity Provider)
members.title_draft: V6.8.1 — Authentication with an Identity Provider
members.description: Verify that, if the application supports multiple identity providers (IdPs), the user's identity cannot be spoofed via another supported identity provider (eg.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.8.2 (V6.8 Authentication with an Identity Provider)
members.title_draft: V6.8.2 — Authentication with an Identity Provider
members.description: Verify that the presence and integrity of digital signatures on authentication assertions (for example on JWTs or SAML assertions) are always validated, rejecting any assertions that are unsigned or have invalid signatures.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.8.3 (V6.8 Authentication with an Identity Provider)
members.title_draft: V6.8.3 — Authentication with an Identity Provider
members.description: Verify that SAML assertions are uniquely processed and used only once within the validity period to prevent replay attacks.

members.source_section: Requirement V6.8.4 (V6.8 Authentication with an Identity Provider)
members.title_draft: V6.8.4 — Authentication with an Identity Provider
members.description: Verify that, if an application uses a separate Identity Provider (IdP) and expects specific authentication strength, methods, or recentness for specific functions, the application verifies this using the information returned by the IdP.

Verify that the user's session inactivity timeout and absolute maximum session lifetime are documented, are appropriate in combination with other controls, and that the documentation includes justification for any deviations from NIST SP 800-63B re-authentication requirements.

Verify that all systems that create and manage user sessions as part of a federated identity management ecosystem (such as SSO systems) are documented along with controls to coordinate session lifetimes, termination, and any other conditions that require re-authentication.

members.source_section: Requirement V7.2.4 (V7.2 Fundamental Session Management Security)
members.description: Verify that the application generates a new session token on user authentication, including re-authentication, and terminates the current session token.
Verify that there is an inactivity timeout such that re-authentication is enforced according to risk analysis and documented security decisions.
Verify that there is an absolute maximum session lifetime such that re-authentication is enforced according to risk analysis and documented security decisions.

Verify that the application gives the option to terminate all other active sessions after a successful change or removal of any authentication factor (including password change via reset or recovery and, if present, an MFA settings update).
Verify that all pages that require authentication have easy and visible access to logout functionality.

members.source_section: Requirement V7.5.1 (V7.5 Defenses Against Session Abuse)
members.description: Verify that the application requires full re-authentication before allowing modifications to sensitive account attributes which may affect authentication such as email address, phone number, MFA configuration, or other information used in account recovery.

members.source_section: Requirement V7.5.3 (V7.5 Defenses Against Session Abuse)
members.description: Verify that the application requires further authentication with at least one factor or secondary verification before performing highly sensitive transactions or operations.

Verify that session lifetime and termination between Relying Parties (RPs) and Identity Providers (IdPs) behave as documented, requiring re-authentication as necessary such as when the maximum time between IdP authentication events is reached.
Verify that creation of a session requires either the user's consent or an explicit action, preventing the creation of new application sessions without user interaction.

Verify that the application's documentation defines the environmental and contextual attributes (including but not limited to, time of day, user location, IP address, or device) that are used in the application to make security decisions, including those pertaining to authentication and authorization.

Verify that authentication and authorization documentation defines how environmental and contextual factors are used in decision-making, in addition to function-level, data-specific, and field-level authorization.

Verify that adaptive security controls based on a consumer's environmental and contextual attributes (such as time of day, location, IP address, or device) are implemented for authentication and authorization decisions, as defined in the application's documentation.
Verify that access to an object is based on the originating subject's (e.g.
Verify that the service receiving a token validates the token to be the correct type and is meant for the intended purpose before accepting the token's contents.
Verify that, if the resource server requires specific authentication strength, methods, or recentness, it verifies that the presented access token satisfies these constraints.
The app performs local authentication (e.g., Biometrics, PIN) securely and validates credentials on a remote endpoint when applicable.
SAD (Sensitive Authentication Data) is not retained after authorization, even if encrypted.
All user access to system components is authenticated via at least one of the following: password/passphrase, token, smart card, biometrics.
MFA is implemented for all access into the CDE.
